title: MTDNA HAPLOGROUPS IN BPD
text:
Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a common lung complication in premature
infants, impairing their lung development and long-term respiratory health. Our research
focuses on mitochondrial dysfunction and specific genetic variations called mtDNA
haplogroups, which contribute to the severity of BPD. By investigating the role of mtDNA
haplogroups and exploring potential therapeutic interventions, we aim to develop personalized
strategies that can mitigate the risk of BPD and improve outcomes for premature infants.

title: Comprehensive CRISPR Editing of iPSCs for Dynamic Disease Modeling in Early-Onset Alzheimer's Research
text:
Early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder
that cause cognitive decline and death within 10-15 years of symptom onset, with no
available disease-modifying treatments. This research will develop the first
comprehensive human cellular models of EOAD using innovative multiplex gene editing
technology, enabling simultaneous real-time monitoring of multiple disease pathways and
facilitating the search for therapeutic interventions that target several mechanisms
concurrently. The completion of this project will accelerate our understanding of EOAD
pathophysiology and provide new tools for identifying multi-pathway therapeutic
compounds for this disease.

title: Modulating the PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint to promote antitumor activity of HER2 CAR T cells in patients with sarcoma
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because average years of life lost to pediatric sarcomas has
remained unacceptably low and unchanged over the last three decades, with less than 30% overall survival in
those with relapsed disease. Immunotherapy offers a potential alternative or synergistic approach to
chemotherapy; at the conclusion of this study, we will understand if manipulating immune inhibitory signals in
the tumor microenvironment using immune check point inhibition safely augments the clinical efficacy of chimeric
antigen receptor T cells, and we will prospectively identify factors that improve patient selection and guide
interventions. These findings will contribute to opening research avenues into both the feasibility and biology of
combination immunotherapy approaches, akin to the historical emergence of multi-drug chemotherapy regimens
to improve cancer outcomes.

title: Targeting the ET domain of BET proteins: specificity and selectivity
text:
BET proteins are of great interest to public health for their involvement in: 1) different types of
cancer such as lung, breast, and prostate; and 2) viral infection. Therapeutic design strategies
against these diseases have targeted BET proteins in the last decade but failed due to toxicity
and drug resistance issues. This project aims to characterize a promising alternative region of
BET proteins to lay the foundation for novel therapeutic strategies that will overcome current
limitations.

title: Core 2: Bioinformatics/Biostatistics/Genomics
text:
Core 2, Bioinformatics / Biostatistics / Genomics Core will provide unified support and consolidation of all the
Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Genomics, Transcriptomics, and Computational Biology relevant to the to the
projects. These tools and resources will be made available to the Cancer Research community and will be useful
to researchers working in the field and to perform similar analyses in other cancer and conditions.

title: ADRC Consortium for Clarity in ADRD Research Through Imaging
text:
Multiple etiologies variously contribute to the clinical syndrome of mild cognitive impairment and dementia
presumed due to Alzheimer’s disease, but the many factors that give rise to symptoms are difficult to quantify at
the level of the individual. A comprehensive panel of imaging and plasma biomarkers will improve the likelihood
that etiologies beyond Alzheimer’s disease can be detected. Such individual-level characterization will greatly
impact diagnostic accuracy, and prediction of symptom course and response to experimental therapies.

title: Elucidating the Role of Biomechanical Strain in Atrial Physiology and Arrhythmias
text:
Atrial fibrillation (AF), estimated to affect 10% of the population over 80, causes significant morbidity and
mortality. Despite this, treatment options for AF are insufficient, and current interventions, which are limited by
side effects and iatrogenic complications, target symptoms and complications rather than the underlying cause.
Understanding the pathogenesis of AF through the biomechanical regulation of its tissue substrate will help
discover novel pathways that can be targeted to more effectively modify the natural course of the disease.

title: Unraveling the molecular mechanisms of innate immune memory in humans
text: In this project we propose to use an inter-disciplinary approach that combines cutting-edge genomic techniques with immunological, epigenetics, and computational tools, to study the molecular mechanisms associated with the induction of long-term innate immune memory in humans.

title: Next-Generation Ultra-high Resolution Ion Mobility Spectrometer for Metabolomics
text: This project aims to create an innovative platform that utilizes ultra-high resolution ion mobility separations in combination with mass spectrometry, which will significantly enhance metabolomics research. The new instrument will have a wide range of clinical and biomedical applications, significantly improving metabolites' identification coverage, sensitivity, and overall data quality than currently achievable.

title: Dual-tracer multiparametric imaging with a long-axial field-of-view PET to better characterize cancer
text:
Numerous new PET radiotracers have improved our ability to image disease. In this project, we develop novel
methods to image two PET radiotracers in the same imaging session as opposed to over days as is currently
done. These new techniques will advance the capabilities of PET to characterize and guide treatment in
oncology.

title: Optimizing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to treat non-malignant disease
text:
Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) with autologous gene therapy is a promising approach to
treating non-malignant blood diseases; however, optimization of stem cell mobilization, transplant conditioning
regimens, and stable engraftment of gene-edited hematopoietic stem cells is essential to maximizing the
curative potential of HSCT. This proposal seeks to overcome these major barriers by investigating novel stem
cell mobilization and antibody-based transplant conditioning strategies and leveraging these approaches to
improve therapy of sickle cell disease. These studies will yield novel insights that will advance the basic
science and translational potential of autologous gene therapy.

title: Mechanisms of hyperactive Ras signaling in craniofacial and dental diseases
text:
The RASopathies are a group of syndromes caused by mutations in components of the Ras/mitogen-activated
protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. These syndromes share many overlapping characteristics, including
structural birth defects in the craniofacial system. The overall goal of this proposal is to better understand the
developmental causes of tooth and skull defects in the RASopathies and to lay a foundation for innovative ther-
apeutic approaches.

title: Isolation of brain reward circuits using peptidergic systems
text:
Perturbations within the dopamine neurotransmitter system of the brain is broadly linked to
neurological disorders, mental illness, and addiction. The way distinct dopamine systems are
regulated at the circuit, molecular, and pharmacological level remains poorly resolved. We will
use advanced genetic and pharmacological techniques to determine how dopamine subsystems
within the ventral tegmental area are regulated that will provide important insights for
therapeutics development.

title: Circuit Engagement in Prosthetically Driven Retina
text:
A significant portion of patients suffering from irreversible blindness could benefit from prosthetic
vision restoration. We can design better retinal prosthetics if we understand how electrical stimulation
from subretinal prosthetics activates early retinal circuits, and if we understand how spared
computational circuits are altered during retinal degeneration. The results from this proposal will inform
biologically rational strategies for stimulating retina to maximize vision restoration.

title: Cell Imaging Core
text: VDDRC Cell Imaging Core The Vanderbilt Digestive Disease Research Center (VDDRC) Cell Imaging Core, operated by the Cell Imaging Shared Resource (CISR), ensures that VDDRC-affiliated investigators have full access to state-of-the-art imaging equipment and expert technical support to conduct sophisticated microscopy and analysis of digestive disease tissue and samples. By utilizing a large, well-established facility, the VDDRC Cell Imaging Core provides high levels of quality control, a dedicated, expert staff and a significant economy of scale for services that would be difficult (if not impossible) for individual investigators to establish and support. This organizational structure fits well with the centralized approach to prevent needless duplication of scientific resources within federally funded research centers, enabling focused development of technology that serves VDDRC investigators. The overall goal of the VDDRC Cell Imaging Core is to provide the full range of modern microscopy and digital imaging capabilities and techniques to enable and accelerate digestive disease research at Vanderbilt through three objectives: 1) acquire and maintain state-of-the art optical and EM imaging technology; 2) train, assist, and encourage VDDRC-affiliated investigators to incorporate optical, EM, and in vivo imaging technologies into their research; and 3) develop new imaging technologies that will be useful for digestive disease research. VDDRC support reduces the net cost of imaging services to VDDRC investigators and has helped provide financial stability essential to sustain historically high levels of service, which has been vital to the successful acquisition of new instruments and services that support VDDRC researchers. During the current funding period, investigators representing 63 separate VDDRC-affiliated laboratories have used all aspects of this Core, leading to 154 peer-reviewed publications. Over the same time period, initiatives taken to obtain equipment grants, combined with institutional contributions, have provided over $4.1M in new capital equipment for the benefit of VDDRC investigators. This includes one commercial and two custom-built lightsheet microscopes, a new confocal microscope, and significant upgrades to both light and electron microscopes. Currently, the VDDRC Cell Imaging Core manages 18 light and electron microscopes valued in excess of $10M, including a Nikon Center of Excellence. The Vanderbilt shared facilities system provides an efficient billing system, oversight and governance for this Core at no extra cost to VDDRC members. The VDDRC Cell Imaging Core will continue to be a critical component in Vanderbilt’s broad range of digestive disease research resources and will provide essential services that support the research of VDDRC-affiliated investigators during the next funding cycle.

title: Molecular determinants of lipid-protein recognition
text:
Lipid headgroups are integral to cellular homeostasis and signaling. Their dysregulation gives rise to a host of
diseases ranging from cardiovascular disease to neurodegeneration. This project will investigate both the
proteins that interact with these lipids and how mis trafficking of these lipids contributes to these diseases.

title: Reciprocal genetics of recently-evolved vertebrate immunity and helminth counter-adaptation
text:
MODIFIED PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
Inflammation can result in the irreversible buildup of fibrosis, an extracellular matrix of collagen and
fibrinogen that contributes to a wide variety of chronic and lethal diseases in humans. The proposed
research will help identify genes and immune pathways that contribute to natural genetic variation in
the risk of fibrosis onset, the severity of fibrosis, and vertebrates’ ability to recover from fibrosis.
Concurrently, we seek to identify strategies that parasitic tapeworms use to interfere with animals’
fibrosis, which may present opportunities for therapeutic interventions to treat, or promote recovery
from, peritoneal fibrosis.

title: Designer nanodiscs to probe and reprogram membrane biology
text:
Proper intercellular signaling is essential for homeostasis and centers on the biochemical reactions at the cell
surface. Armed with innovative nanotechnology, the proposed study will decipher the molecular underpinnings
of cell-cell interactions that are unapproachable using traditional methods, thereby shedding light on new ideas
to manipulate membrane biology involved in human health.

title: Integration of HSC Stress Responses and Disease Progression by DNMT3A Mutations
text:
Defective hematopoiesis is a hallmark of blood diseases, many of which are enriched with Dnmt3a mutations
and are associated with an enhanced inflammatory milieu. This project will generate an improved understanding
of the mechanism(s) by which Dnmt3a mutations endow a fitness advantage to hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs)
during chronic inflammation, which remodels bone marrow composition and reinforces further selections of the
mutant HSCs for disease progression. Results generated from this study will likely lead to therapeutic
opportunities that allow early interventions of DNMT3A-mutant clonal hematopoiesis-associated blood diseases.

title: Internet-delivered mindfulness training to reduce cognitive variability in adults with subjective cognitive decline
text:
There is a critical need to identify behavioral interventions to promote neurocognitive stability among
individuals at-risk for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) and related dementias. The proposed research will build upon
a pilot feasibility trial (1R61AG081982-01) to examine preliminary effects of an internet-delivered mindfulness
training program on everyday cognitive variability and intrinsic brain dynamics in adults with subjective
cognitive decline. Specifically, this proposal will assess preliminary effects of the training programs on
everyday cognitive variability using ecological momentary assessment cognitive testing and on whole-brain
dynamic states using resting-state dynamic functional connectivity.
